children: The U.S. Treasury Department will buy up to $6B of 10- to 20-year Treasury bonds in a buyback operation on Thursday, tripling the size of its previous long-dated purchase as it seeks to support liquidity in the government bond market.
The move comes after a recent selloff pushed longer-term Treasury yields sharply higher, with the 30-year yield reaching its highest level since 2007.

The Treasury said last month it would at least double the size of its buybacks of longer-dated securities to $4B per operation over the next quarter. The latest operation goes beyond that commitment, with purchases of up to $6B.

The announcement did little to ease pressure in the bond market, with the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield rising to 4.8528%, its highest level since November 2023, after the buyback plan was announced.

The 10-year Treasury yield was down 0.4 basis point at 4.831%, while the 20-year yield fell 0.2 basis point to 5.285% at press time. The modest moves suggested that the Treasury's $6B buyback announcement had yet to produce a meaningful easing in long-term borrowing costs.

title: U.S. Treasury boosts September 10 bond buyback to $6B
